BiblicalUsage: Pantē means in every way, wholly, always. Tertullus flatters Felix, saying, We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this one flattering word warns me: always and in all places sounds like praise, but it opens a speech meant to condemn an innocent man.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
